issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/Pduhard/expo-router-dismissto-params (with pnpm patch on the with-fix branch)

### Steps to reproduce

Root Stack with `index`, `[id]` and `modal`.

`pnpm install && pnpm exec playwright install chromium && pnpm test` 
Open `/`
press **router.push('/1')**
press **router.push('/modal')**
Press **router.dismissTo('/2')**
Press **router.back()**

**Expected:** `/2` is not in the history, so step 4 replaces `modal` with `/2`, and Back returns to `/1`. The same calls inside a `(group)` stack already do this ([dismissTo.test.ios.tsx#L483](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/0e673ace1aa2981e08d48290c98377433c9e9282/packages/expo-router/src/__tests__/dismissTo.test.ios.tsx#L483)).

**Actual:** step 4 pops to `/1` and overwrites its params with `{ id: '2' }`. `/1` is gone, and Back goes to `/`.

- Any stack that gets the `POP_TO` directly does it.
- Same with a dynamic layout (seen in Jest): `[slug]/(group)/_layout` + `[slug]/details`, `push('/a')`, `push('/a/details')`, `dismissTo('/b')` pops to `a`'s group and gives it `slug: 'b'`.
- Same with `<Link dismissTo>`.

Checked with `expo-router@58.0.30` on web and in the Jest `.ios` suite on `main`.

**Cause:** without `dangerouslySingular`, the `POP_TO` loop pops to the last route with the same name, whatever its path params ([StackRouter.tsx#L581-L590](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/0e673ace1aa2981e08d48290c98377433c9e9282/packages/expo-router/src/react-navigation/routers/StackRouter.tsx#L581-L590)).


Question: should `dismissTo` match the path params (like the docs and the `(group)` test), or only the route name (like a direct stack today)?


### Environment

```text

    System:
      OS: Linux 7.0 Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
      Shell: 5.9 - /usr/bin/zsh

      expo: ~58.0.23 => 58.0.23
      expo-router: 58.0.30 => 58.0.30
      react: 19.3.0 => 19.3.0
      react-dom: 19.3.0 => 19.3.0
      react-native: 0.88.1 => 0.88.1
```


issue.title: [Worklets 0.13.0] Startup crash on Expo SDK 58 / RN 0.88: native proxy exposes loadUnpackers instead of loadUnpackersWithCode

labels.name: repo-85b6f9f6
labels.description: This issue need minimum repro scenario

labels.name: repo-85b6f9f6
labels.description: This issue is specific to iOS

issue.body:
### Description

After upgrading to Expo SDK 58 (React Native 0.88, `react-native-worklets` 0.13.0, Reanimated 4.7.1) the app crashes on startup in a debug build on the iOS simulator:

```
TypeError: undefined is not a function
  installUnpackers (react-native-worklets/src/WorkletsModule/NativeWorklets.native.ts:459:46)
  constructor (react-native-worklets/src/WorkletsModule/NativeWorklets.native.ts:39:25)
  <global> (react-native-worklets/src/WorkletsModule/NativeWorklets.native.ts:428:66)
  <global> (react-native-worklets/src/memory/serializable.native.ts:10)
  <global> (react-native-worklets/src/initializers/initializers.native.ts:8)
```

`installUnpackers` calls `workletsModuleProxy.loadUnpackersWithCode(...)`, but the native proxy installed on the RN runtime does not have that method. Logging the proxy right before `installUnpackers`:

```js
const p = globalThis.__workletsModuleProxy;
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(p).filter((k) => k.includes('npack'));
// [["loadUnpackers", 13, "function"]]
typeof p.loadUnpackersWithCode; // "undefined"
typeof p.loadUnpackers;         // "function"
```

So at runtime the proxy exposes the old `loadUnpackers` method (the pre-0.13 API, as in #9600) instead of `loadUnpackersWithCode` / `loadUnpackersWithBytecode`, while the JS side is 0.13.0.

What we checked:
- `node_modules/react-native-worklets` is 0.13.0 (single copy), `Podfile.lock` has `RNWorklets (0.13.0)`.
- The Metro bundle contains only `loadUnpackersWithCode` / `loadUnpackersWithBytecode`.
- In the built `libRNWorklets.a`, `JSIWorkletsModuleProxy.o` contains the strings `loadUnpackersWithCode` and `loadUnpackersWithBytecode`. However the linked `<App>.debug.dylib` also contains a `loadUnpackers` C-string, which `react-native-worklets` 0.13.0 sources do not have — so it looks like an older `JSIWorkletsModuleProxy` implementation ends up linked/used at runtime.
- The pod graph also has `ExpoModulesWorklets (58.0.24)` (prebuilt xcframework) and `ExpoModulesWorkletsAdapter (58.0.24)` from `expo-modules-core`, which depend on `RNWorklets`; we suspect a duplicate/older worklets definition coming through that path, but could not confirm.
- Fully clean rebuild does not help: removed `ios/`, `android/`, `.expo`, DerivedData, Metro/haste caches, CocoaPods cache for RNWorklets, `watchman watch-del-all`, uninstalled the app, `expo prebuild --clean`, `expo run:ios`, `expo start --clear`. Same crash.
- The same project on Expo SDK 57 (RN 0.86, worklets 0.10.1, Reanimated 4.5.1) works.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Expo app on SDK 57 using Reanimated 4.5 / Worklets 0.10 (`react-native-worklets/plugin` in `babel.config.js`).
2. `npx expo install expo@^58.0.0 --fix` (→ RN 0.88.0, Reanimated 4.7.1, Worklets 0.13.0).
3. `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform ios && npx expo run:ios` on an iOS 26.5 simulator (Xcode 26.6).
4. `npx expo start --dev-client --clear` and open the app → crash above on startup.

### Snack or a link to a repository

Private app, no minimal repro yet. Happy to run any additional diagnostics.

### Reanimated version

4.7.1

### Worklets version

0.13.0

### React Native version

0.88.0 (Expo SDK 58.0.17, expo-modules-core 58.0.24)

### Platforms

iOS

### JavaScript runtime

Hermes

### Workflow

Expo Dev Client (CNG, `expo prebuild`)

### Architecture

New Architecture

### Build type

Debug app & dev bundle

### Device

iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.5)

### Host machine

macOS (Apple Silicon), Xcode 26.6, Node 24.11

- SDK 57 app (Reanimated 4.5.1, Worklets 0.10.1, `expo-dev-client`, `react-native-worklets/plugin` in babel) → works
- `npx expo install expo@^58.0.0` + `--fix` (Reanimated 4.7.1, Worklets 0.13.0), `expo prebuild --clean`, `expo run:ios` → app starts, animation runs

My `.debug.dylib` only has `loadUnpackersWithCode` / `loadUnpackersWithBytecode`, no bare `loadUnpackers`. So I'd guess something in your setup still pulls in an older worklets build, but I can't tell what from here.


issue.title: [miniflare] Handle client socket errors in the Hyperdrive proxy
issue.body: Fixes #15768. The Hyperdrive proxy has no `error` listener on the client socket, so a client socket error crashes the Node process. Two windows, plus one leak: - **After the pipes:** `pipe()` re-emits a client error when nothing else listens, so it still crashes. Every pipe site now goes through `pipeSockets`, which tears down both ends on error. - **During negotiation (TLS paths):** the client socket has no listener before the pipes exist. One is attached when the connection is accepted. - **Leak on the fallback paths:** the database socket can open after the client has errored, and then stays open. `pipeSockets` destroys it at once. No test: that window can't be made deterministic. `pipeSockets` replaces `setupTLSConnection`. `createPlainTCPConnection` no longer sets its own error handler, so it drops its `clientSocket` parameter. `proxy.spec.ts` covers the two windows: both tests fail on `main` and pass here. --- - Tests - [x] Tests included/updated - [ ] Automated tests not possible - manual testing has been completed as follows: - [ ] Additional testing not necessary because: - Public documentation - [ ] Cloudflare docs PR(s): - [x] Documentation not necessary because: internal socket lifecycle change, no public API surface touched. > [!NOTE] > This is a contribution from an AI agent: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5. A human reviewed the diff and ran the reproduction, but wrote neither the patch nor this description. ---

comment.body: Closing: main no longer crashes here. Both tests from this PR pass after #15879 and #14900. Thanks for the review :)

issue.title: [Web] 15.16.0 breaks Vite/rolldown builds: "TurboModuleRegistry" is not exported by react-native-web (NativeSvgSoundModule)

comment.body:
Repro: https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-svg-web-vite (Vite 8, pnpm, `pnpm install && pnpm build`).

- 15.15.4 builds, 15.16.0 fails with `"TurboModuleRegistry" is not exported by react-native-web`, on React Native 0.86 and 0.88 alike (`./matrix.sh`).
- `SvgTouchableMixin` requires `../fabric/NativeSvgSoundModule` inside an Android-only branch, but the bundler still follows the `require`, and Rolldown fails on the missing export.
- Branch `with-fix` moves the call into `lib/playTouchSound.android.ts`, with a no-op `lib/playTouchSound.ts`, the same split as `resolveAssetUri.ts` / `resolveAssetUri.web.ts`. The build passes and the page renders. The sound module still never loads on iOS, as with today's lazy `require`.

issue.title: [Web] @react-native/assets-registry is still imported on web but not declared, so it cannot be resolved with React Native 0.87+

labels.name: repo-b3c2f7d1
labels.description: The user didn't precise the problem enough

issue.body:
### Description

#3076 fixed #3015 for native by moving the `@react-native/assets-registry/registry` import into `src/lib/resolveAssetUri.web.ts`. On web, though, the import is still always loaded: `src/web/utils/prepare.ts` imports `resolveAssetUri`, so even a plain `<Svg><Circle /></Svg>` needs it. `@react-native/assets-registry` is not in react-native-svg's `dependencies` or `peerDependencies`. react-native-web does not depend on it, and react-native 0.87+ no longer does either. So in a fresh web project the import cannot be resolved, even with npm hoisting:

```
Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "@react-native/assets-registry/registry" from ".../node_modules/react-native-svg/lib/module/lib/resolveAssetUri.web.js".
This is most likely unintended because it can break your application at runtime.
```

This is the same web problem as #2418 (introduced in 15.5.0, closed without a fix). It becomes more common now that React Native itself no longer installs the package. Users currently have to add `@react-native/assets-registry` to their own dependencies, or alias it to `react-native-web/dist/modules/AssetRegistry` (see https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-svg/issues/2418#issuecomment-6036147638).

Expected: react-native-svg works on web without extra, undeclared packages.
Actual: the build fails unless the app installs `@react-native/assets-registry` itself.

Suggested fix: react-native 0.87+ exports `AssetRegistry` publicly, and react-native-web 0.21.4 added the matching export (necolas/react-native-web#2885). So `resolveAssetUri.web.ts` could use:

```ts
import { AssetRegistry } from 'react-native';
// ...
const asset = AssetRegistry.getAssetByID(source);
```

I checked locally that this builds with `@react-native/assets-registry` uninstalled (react-native-web 0.21.4). It also reads assets from the registry react-native-web uses. The tradeoff: react-native-web before 0.21.4 does not export `AssetRegistry`, so this needs either a minimum react-native-web version or a fallback. Another option is to declare `@react-native/assets-registry` as a (possibly optional) peer dependency so package managers at least report it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the `package.json`, `vite.config.js` and `src/main.jsx` from #3086, but remove `@react-native/assets-registry` from `dependencies`. To see this error on 15.16.0 you also need to work around #3086, for example with the stub plugin described there. On 15.15.5 the same error shows directly.
2. `npm install` (npm installs react-native 0.88.0 as the peer, which no longer brings in `@react-native/assets-registry`).
3. `npm run build`: fails with the error above.
4. `npm i -E @react-native/assets-registry@0.88.0`, then `npm run build`: succeeds.

### Snack or a link to a repository

Inline (see steps). It is web-only, so a Snack does not apply.

### SVG version

15.16.0 (also 15.15.5, and every version since 15.5.0)

### React Native version

react-native-web 0.21.4, react-native 0.88.0

### Platforms

Web

### JavaScript runtime

V8 (Chrome)

### Workflow

Other: Vite 8.3.4 (rolldown) + react-native-web

### Architecture

N/A (web)

### Build type

Production bundle (`vite build`)

### Device

N/A. Node 26.12.0, npm 11.20.0, macOS.

comment.body:
Repro: https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-svg-web-vite (Vite 8, pnpm).

- With React Native 0.88, `lib/resolveAssetUri.web.js` cannot resolve `@react-native/assets-registry/registry`: react-native-svg does not declare it, and React Native stopped depending on it in 0.87. With 0.86 it resolves through react-native's dependency.
- `./matrix.sh` shows it past the #3086 error (`shimMissingExports`).
- Adding `@react-native/assets-registry` to react-native-svg's `dependencies` fixes it: branch `with-fix`.

issue.title: [miniflare] Hyperdrive proxy crashes the Node process when the client socket errors

labels.name: repo-2a70fd9f
labels.description: Relating to Miniflare

labels.name: repo-2a70fd9f
labels.description: Relating to Cloudflare Hyperdrive: https://developers.cloudflare.com/hyperdrive/

issue.body:
### What versions & operating system are you using?

```
  System:
    OS: Linux 7.0 Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
    CPU: (32) x64 AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor
    Memory: 16.45 GB / 30.45 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.9 - /usr/bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 22.14.0
    npm: 10.9.2
    pnpm: 11.24.0
  npmPackages:
    miniflare: 4.20260730.0 => 4.20260730.0
```

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction

https://github.com/Pduhard/miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro

### Describe the Bug

The local Hyperdrive proxy pipes the workerd client socket to the database socket. Only the database side gets an `error` listener.

In `packages/miniflare/src/plugins/hyperdrive/hyperdrive-proxy.ts` on `main`:

- `createPlainTCPConnection` attaches `dbSocket.on("error", ...)`
- `setupTLSConnection` attaches `tlsSocket.on("error", ...)`
- `clientSocket` gets nothing, at any of the four places it is piped: `#handleConnection`, `handlePostgresTlsConnection`, `handleMySQLTlsConnection`, `setupTLSConnection`. It also gets nothing before those pipes exist: on the TLS paths, `#handleConnection` writes to the database, reads the reply and runs a TLS handshake first, and a client that resets during that window crashes the process the same way

`pipe()` does not cover this. It attaches an `onerror` handler to the destination, but that handler removes itself and re-emits once no other listener is left. So when the client socket errors after the pipes are set up, nothing is listening, and the whole Node process exits. That takes down `wrangler dev`, `getPlatformProxy()`, or a vitest run.

**Steps to reproduce**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Pduhard/miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro
cd miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro
npm install
npm run repro:half-close
npm run repro:reset
```

`repro:half-close` runs a TCP server that speaks just enough of the Postgres protocol to negotiate TLS, then streams data. A Worker connects through a Hyperdrive binding and half-closes its socket while that data is still arriving. Nothing reaches into Miniflare internals.

`repro:reset` covers the other window: it talks to the proxy port directly and resets the connection while the proxy is still negotiating TLS with the database, before any pipe exists.

Expected: the connection is torn down and Miniflare keeps running.
Observed: the process exits 1 on an uncaught error.

**Which configurations reach this code**

Since #13390 the proxy is skipped when `sslmode=disable`, so that mode no longer reaches it. `require`, `prefer`, `verify-ca` and `verify-full` still do, which is the ordinary setup for developing locally against a hosted Postgres that requires TLS.

| version | `sslmode=disable` | `sslmode=require` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `4.20260424.0` | exits 1 | exits 1 |
| `4.20260730.0` | 20 of 20 attempts survive | exits 1 |

The same code is on `main` today.

### Please provide any relevant error logs

```
node:events:496
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: write EPIPE
    at WriteWrap.onWriteComplete [as oncomplete] (node:internal/stream_base_commons:87:19)
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at Socket.onerror (node:internal/streams/readable:1028:14)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:518:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:129:3)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:90:21) {
  errno: -32,
  code: 'EPIPE',
  syscall: 'write'
}
```

`Socket.onerror` at `readable.js:1028` is the listener `pipe()` installed on the destination, re-emitting because nothing else was listening. Depending on whether the write lands just before or just after the peer's FIN, the same failure also shows up as `Error: This socket has been ended by the other party` at `Socket.writeAfterFIN`.

---

PR: #15769. It attaches the listener as soon as the connection is accepted and at each pipe site, with a regression test for each of the two windows in `packages/miniflare/test/plugins/hyperdrive/proxy.spec.ts`. Both tests fail on `main`.

comment.body: Fixed on main by the proxy rework (#15879, #14900): a client socket error mid-stream or a reset during negotiation no longer takes down the process. Checked by running the two tests from #15769 against main.

issue.title: Android: a ClipPath's cached path is never rebuilt when its Rect children change props
issue.body:
### Description

On Android, a `<ClipPath>` whose child shapes change their props (e.g. a `<Rect y={…} height={…}>` recomputed from new data) keeps clipping with the geometry of the first draw. The clipped element itself and every other shape in the `<Svg>` re-render correctly; only the clip is stale. The clip updates again after an `<Svg>` prop change (width/viewBox) or a full remount. iOS is not affected.

**Why (traced in 15.15.4):**

- `ClipPathView extends GroupView`; `GroupView.getPath(canvas, paint)` caches `mPath` and returns it on every later call (`android/src/main/java/com/horcrux/svg/GroupView.java`, `getPath`).
- `VirtualView.getClipPath(canvas, paint)` uses that cached variant whenever `mClipRule == CLIP_RULE_EVENODD` (`VirtualView.java`). `mClipRule` is an `int` field whose default is `0 == CLIP_RULE_EVENODD`, and the JS side only sends `clipRule` when the prop is set (`src/lib/extract/extractProps.ts`), so every element without an explicit `clipRule` takes the cached branch.
- Children of a `ClipPath` are never drawn (`ClipPathView.draw` only logs), so a child `RectView`'s `mPath` stays `null`. `VirtualView.invalidate()` returns early for a `RenderableView` whose `mPath == null` (`VirtualView.java`, `invalidate`) — before `clearParentCache()` — so a prop update on that child never clears the `ClipPath`'s cached `mPath`.
- iOS: `RNSVGNode.invalidate` propagates to the superview container and clears its path unconditionally (`apple/RNSVGNode.mm`), so the group path is rebuilt.

**Suggested fix:** `VirtualView.invalidate()` should not early-return for a never-drawn `RenderableView` when it has a parent whose path cache may hold it (or `RectView`/shape `setX/Y/Width/Height` should call `clearParentCache()` explicitly). Alternatively the JS side could always send `clipRule` (SVG's default is `nonzero`, not `evenodd`), which would both match the spec default and route clips through the uncached branch.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Render the component below (one `Svg` with a `Defs` > `ClipPath` > `Rect`, a band `Rect`, and a `Path` drawn twice — once plain, once clipped by the `ClipPath`).
2. Note where the red part of the line ends: at the band's top edge (y = 40).
3. Press **move band**: `top` becomes 120, the band `Rect` moves down.
4. Android: the red part of the line still ends at y = 40. iOS: it ends at the band's new edge (y = 120).
5. Press again: on Android nothing about the clip ever changes; a full remount of the `Svg` (or any `Svg` prop change such as `width`) refreshes it once.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, View } from "react-native";
import Svg, { ClipPath, Defs, Path, Rect } from "react-native-svg";

export default function Repro() {
  const [top, setTop] = useState(40);
  return (
    <View>
      <Button title="move band" onPress={() => setTop((t) => (t === 40 ? 120 : 40))} />
      <Svg width={300} height={200} viewBox="0 0 300 200">
        <Defs>
          <ClipPath id="above">
            {/* region above the band: y=0 .. top */}
            <Rect x={0} y={0} width={300} height={top} />
          </ClipPath>
        </Defs>
        {/* the band itself, drawn directly — always follows `top` */}
        <Rect x={0} y={top} width={300} height={40} fill="#2563eb" fillOpacity={0.15} />
        {/* a diagonal line, red only where it is above the band */}
        <Path d="M0 200 L300 0" stroke="#999" strokeWidth={3} />
        <Path d="M0 200 L300 0" stroke="#d03b3b" strokeWidth={3} clipPath="url(#above)" />
      </Svg>
    </View>
  );
}
```

Expected: after "move band", the red part of the line ends at the band's new top edge.
Actual (Android): the band moves, the red part still ends at the old edge (y = 40 or 120, whichever was drawn first).
Workarounds that confirm the cause: (a) give the `<ClipPath>` a `key` that changes with `top` (new native node, empty cache); (b) set `clipRule="nonzero"` on the clipped `<Path>` (takes the uncached `getPath(canvas, paint, Region.Op.UNION)` branch).

### Snack or a link to a repository

https://github.com/warlock1987/rnsvg-clippath-repro — a blank Expo SDK 57 app whose `App.tsx` is the component above (react-native-svg 15.15.4, RN 0.86, Fabric, Hermes). `npm install && npx expo run:android`, press **move band**.

### SVG version

15.15.4

### React Native version

0.86.0 (Expo SDK 57)

### Platforms

Android

### JavaScript runtime

Hermes

### Workflow

Expo Dev Client

### Architecture

Fabric (New Architecture)

### Build type

Debug app & dev bundle

### Device

Android emulator

### Device model

Pixel 10 emulator (Android 17, Google APIs image); also reproduced on an EAS development build. Not reproducible on the iOS 18 Simulator.

Yes

issue.title: [Worklets][Web] Vitest is taken for Jest, so `requestAnimationFrame` becomes a `setTimeout`

labels.name: repo-85b6f9f6
labels.description: This issue is specific to web

labels.name: repo-85b6f9f6
labels.description: A reproduction with a snippet of code, snack or repo is provided

issue.body:
### Description

Since #9703, Worklets and Reanimated take Vitest for Jest, in jsdom and in browser mode (a real Chromium) alike:

```ts
// packages/react-native-worklets/src/platformChecker.ts
// packages/react-native-reanimated/src/common/constants/platform.ts
export const IS_JEST: boolean =
  typeof globalThis.jest !== 'undefined' || process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test';
```

- Jest puts `jest` in each module's scope, not on `globalThis`, so `typeof globalThis.jest` is always `'undefined'` and only `NODE_ENV === 'test'` matches.
- Vitest sets `NODE_ENV=test` too (`process.env.NODE_ENV ??= 'test'`). It sets neither `JEST_WORKER_ID` nor a `jest` global, so before #9703 it was not taken for Jest.

On the web this runs the Jest setup outside Jest:

- Worklets `init()` replaces the page's `requestAnimationFrame` with `mockedRequestAnimationFrame` (`setTimeout(cb, 0)`), and `runOnUI` schedules through it.
- Reanimated runs its mappers synchronously and `getStaticFeatureFlag` returns `false`. On `main`, `initializeWebGlobals()` also replaces `requestAnimationFrame`.

A test that fakes `setTimeout` (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout'] })`) then gets no frame: animations stop and `await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)` hangs.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test        # browser + jsdom: 4 of 6 fail on 0.11.0 – 0.13.0, 6/6 pass on 0.10.4
pnpm test:jest   # under Jest: typeof jest === 'object', typeof globalThis.jest === 'undefined'
```

```ts
test("importing react-native-worklets keeps the browser's requestAnimationFrame", async () => {
  const browserRaf = window.requestAnimationFrame;
  await import('react-native-worklets');
  expect(window.requestAnimationFrame).toBe(browserRaf); // got mockedRequestAnimationFrame
});

test('a frame still comes once setTimeout is faked', async () => {
  await import('react-native-worklets');
  vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout'] });
  await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame); // times out
});
```

### Snack or a link to a repository

https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-worklets-vitest-raf (Vitest 5, browser mode with Playwright and jsdom, no React Native, no Reanimated)

### Possible fix

```ts
export const IS_JEST: boolean = typeof jest !== 'undefined';
```

in both files. Jest passes `jest` to every module it loads (jest-runtime's module wrapper), React Native's Jest setup calls it, Vitest does not define it, and no bundler can inline it (#9703's `react-native-dotenv` case). This brings back the pre-#9703 result for Vitest. Jest with `injectGlobals: false` or native ESM has no bare `jest`; React Native's preset needs `injectGlobals`.

Checked on `main`: Worklets 107/107 and Reanimated 1972 Jest tests pass with it (forcing `IS_JEST = false` fails 110 of 121 Reanimated suites), `type:check:src:native` and `:web` and `oxlint` are clean, and branch `with-fix` of the repro passes 6/6. A PR is ready if you want it.

### Reanimated version

4.5.0 – 4.7.1, `main`

### Worklets version

0.11.0 – 0.13.0, `main`

### React Native version

0.88.0 (web, react-native-web 0.21.4)

### Platforms

Web

### JavaScript runtime

None (Chromium, Vitest browser mode)

### Workflow

Expo Dev Client

### Acknowledgements

Yes

issue.title: [miniflare] Hyperdrive proxy crashes the Node process when the client socket errors

labels.name: repo-2a70fd9f
labels.description: Relating to Miniflare

labels.name: repo-2a70fd9f
labels.description: Relating to Cloudflare Hyperdrive: https://developers.cloudflare.com/hyperdrive/

issue.body:
### What versions & operating system are you using?

```
  System:
    OS: Linux 7.0 Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
    CPU: (32) x64 AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor
    Memory: 16.45 GB / 30.45 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.9 - /usr/bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 22.14.0
    npm: 10.9.2
    pnpm: 11.24.0
  npmPackages:
    miniflare: 4.20260730.0 => 4.20260730.0
```

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction

https://github.com/Pduhard/miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro

### Describe the Bug

The local Hyperdrive proxy pipes the workerd client socket to the database socket. Only the database side gets an `error` listener.

In `packages/miniflare/src/plugins/hyperdrive/hyperdrive-proxy.ts` on `main`:

- `createPlainTCPConnection` attaches `dbSocket.on("error", ...)`
- `setupTLSConnection` attaches `tlsSocket.on("error", ...)`
- `clientSocket` gets nothing, at any of the four places it is piped: `#handleConnection`, `handlePostgresTlsConnection`, `handleMySQLTlsConnection`, `setupTLSConnection`. It also gets nothing before those pipes exist: on the TLS paths, `#handleConnection` writes to the database, reads the reply and runs a TLS handshake first, and a client that resets during that window crashes the process the same way

`pipe()` does not cover this. It attaches an `onerror` handler to the destination, but that handler removes itself and re-emits once no other listener is left. So when the client socket errors after the pipes are set up, nothing is listening, and the whole Node process exits. That takes down `wrangler dev`, `getPlatformProxy()`, or a vitest run.

**Steps to reproduce**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Pduhard/miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro
cd miniflare-hyperdrive-crash-repro
npm install
npm run repro:half-close
npm run repro:reset
```

`repro:half-close` runs a TCP server that speaks just enough of the Postgres protocol to negotiate TLS, then streams data. A Worker connects through a Hyperdrive binding and half-closes its socket while that data is still arriving. Nothing reaches into Miniflare internals.

`repro:reset` covers the other window: it talks to the proxy port directly and resets the connection while the proxy is still negotiating TLS with the database, before any pipe exists.

Expected: the connection is torn down and Miniflare keeps running.
Observed: the process exits 1 on an uncaught error.

**Which configurations reach this code**

Since #13390 the proxy is skipped when `sslmode=disable`, so that mode no longer reaches it. `require`, `prefer`, `verify-ca` and `verify-full` still do, which is the ordinary setup for developing locally against a hosted Postgres that requires TLS.

| version | `sslmode=disable` | `sslmode=require` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `4.20260424.0` | exits 1 | exits 1 |
| `4.20260730.0` | 20 of 20 attempts survive | exits 1 |

The same code is on `main` today.

### Please provide any relevant error logs

```
node:events:496
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: write EPIPE
    at WriteWrap.onWriteComplete [as oncomplete] (node:internal/stream_base_commons:87:19)
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at Socket.onerror (node:internal/streams/readable:1028:14)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:518:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:129:3)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:90:21) {
  errno: -32,
  code: 'EPIPE',
  syscall: 'write'
}
```

`Socket.onerror` at `readable.js:1028` is the listener `pipe()` installed on the destination, re-emitting because nothing else was listening. Depending on whether the write lands just before or just after the peer's FIN, the same failure also shows up as `Error: This socket has been ended by the other party` at `Socket.writeAfterFIN`.

---

PR: #15769. It attaches the listener as soon as the connection is accepted and at each pipe site, with a regression test for each of the two windows in `packages/miniflare/test/plugins/hyperdrive/proxy.spec.ts`. Both tests fail on `main`.

issue.title: [useResponderEvents] A move onto a sibling of the responder never asks their parent
issue.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the issue

A parent `PanResponder` is never asked to take a mouse drag that goes from one child responder onto a sibling child responder. A drag that stays on the first child does ask it.

It only happens when the parent is the outermost view with responder props.

### Expected behavior

The parent is asked, as when the drag stays on the first child.

### Steps to reproduce

react-native-web 0.21.4, Chrome.

```jsx
<View {...panResponder.panHandlers}>
  <View onStartShouldSetResponder={() => true} /> {/* A */}
  <View onStartShouldSetResponder={() => true} /> {/* B */}
</View>
```

Press on `A`, drag onto `B`: `onMoveShouldSetPanResponder` is never called.

### Test case

https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-rnw-responder-lca

### Additional comments

`getLowestCommonAncestor` (`useResponderEvents/utils.js`) reads the first pair twice (`pathA[indexA++]`), so it never compares the last one. Here the last one is the only common ancestor, so it returns `null` and nobody is asked:

```js
getLowestCommonAncestor([1, 0], [2, 0]) // null, expected 0
```

Fix in #2917.

issue.title: [core] Fix the missing expo global on web in Rolldown and Vite 8 builds

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

- Rolldown / `vite build` (Vite 8) on web: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'EventEmitter')`.
- Web `ensureNativeModulesAreInstalled()` is empty and installs the polyfill through `import './polyfill'`. `sideEffects` declares the file pure, so Rolldown removes the call, the file and the polyfill.

# How

- The web function now calls `installExpoGlobalPolyfill()`. This is the pre-#37588 behavior. The installer returns at once when `globalThis.expo` exists.
- Not picked: add the file to `sideEffects` (one more hard-coded path), rename it to `.fx.ts` (changes every importer).

# Test Plan

- New `ensureNativeModulesAreInstalled-test.web.ts`: fails on `main`, passes here.
- `et check-packages expo-modules-core` passes.
- Repro: https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-expo-modules-core-side-effects (Rolldown and Vite 8, SDK 57 and 58: FAIL before, OK after).

# Screenshots

No UI change.

# Checklist

- [x] I added a changeset and followed [this short guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-before-submitting)
- [x] This diff will work correctly for `npx expo prebuild` & EAS Build (eg: updated a module plugin).
- [ ] Conforms with the [Documentation Writing Style Guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/guides/Expo%20Documentation%20Writing%20Style%20Guide.md)

Investigated and written with Claude Code; I reviewed it.

`vp lint` / `vp fmt` run oxlint/oxfmt from a parent directory instead of the bundled one
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

- `vp lint` / `vp fmt` / `vp check` resolve oxlint and oxfmt from the cwd upward; the bundled copy is only the fallback.
- A project that doesn't install oxlint, under a folder with `node_modules/oxlint`, runs the parent's copy (our case: a git worktree inside the main checkout).
- With a parent oxlint ≤ 1.61, the parent's `.oxlintrc.json` applies and the `lint` block of `vite.config.ts` is ignored. No warning.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Pduhard/repro-vite-plus-lint-overrides

### Steps to reproduce

in the repro fork:

```sh
pnpm install          # parent: oxlint 1.60.0
cd app && pnpm install  # app: vite-plus 1.2.0
./node_modules/.bin/vp lint --version  # expected 1.88.0
./node_modules/.bin/vp lint src        # expected 1 error
```

### System Info

```shell
vite-plus 1.2.0, Node 24.17.0, pnpm 12.11.2
Linux x64; also Windows (windows-latest), incl. a parent copy at D:\node_modules
```

### Used Package Manager

pnpm

### Logs

```shell

```
